script: Spread, total, and weather were not saved for Week 4 DAL at HOU, so the script is inferred only from the three-game samples. Dallas has been pass-led, CeeDee Lamb 26 targets for 309 yards and George Pickens 25 targets for 150 yards, with Javonte Williams at 43 carries for 169 yards. Houston has allowed 3.59 rush yards per carry and only 6 runs of 10-plus, so Dallas should not grind Williams and should throw into the 10.11 yards per attempt Houston allows in the middle. Houston's backs are inefficient, David Montgomery 37 carries for 103 yards and Woody Marks 22 carries for 65, but Dallas has allowed 5.23 rush yards per carry and 15 runs of 10-plus, so Houston can run more than its form and still live through Dalton Schultz's 25 targets for 205 yards.
who_goes_off: CeeDee Lamb is the Dallas piece who should go off: 309 receiving yards and 311 air yards on 26 targets over three games, against a Houston defense that has allowed 13 passes of 20-plus yards on 108 attempts and 10.11 yards per attempt in the middle. Dalton Schultz is the Houston piece: 205 receiving yards on 25 targets, into a Dallas defense allowing 9.0 yards per attempt on 17 middle throws, with C.J. Stroud at 0.42 EPA per dropback versus the blitz and Dallas blitzing 27%.
weak_spot: Houston's weak spot is the middle at 10.11 yards per attempt on 27 throws and the right at 9.48 on 42 throws, not the left at 3.89 on 27 throws, so the matchup is Jake Ferguson and CeeDee Lamb in the middle rather than an outside corner. Dallas's weak spot is the run at 5.23 yards per carry allowed and 15 runs of 10-plus, plus the middle at 9.0 yards per attempt on 17 throws, while its right side is the best at 6.84 on 31 throws.
injury_fallout: No injury list was saved for Week 4 DAL at HOU, so no injury fallout is priced. The usage split on the sheet is the fallout proxy: Nico Collins has 10 targets for 75 yards while Dalton Schultz has 25 targets for 205 yards and Xavier Hutchinson has 21 targets for 120 yards on 290 air yards.
qb_vs_blitz: Dak Prescott's EPA per dropback is 0.05 versus the blitz on 44 dropbacks and 0.45 with no blitz, and Houston blitzes only 23%, so most Dallas dropbacks are the look Prescott has crushed. C.J. Stroud's EPA per dropback is 0.42 versus the blitz on 25 dropbacks and -0.13 with no blitz, and Dallas blitzes 27%, so Stroud is good on about one quarter of dropbacks and negative on the rest.

Dalton Schultz has 205 receiving yards in three games, 68.3 per game, versus a 40.5 line, on 25 targets and 157 air yards, and Dallas has allowed 9.0 yards per attempt on 17 middle attempts while C.J. Stroud's 0.42 blitz EPA meets a 27% Dallas blitz rate, ahead of Nico Collins at 10 targets for 75 yards.
